Outbound XML messages that require converting to either Inbound exception messages 
or Inbound "normal" messages can be stored in this directory (dist\jmsutilclient-X.X.X\conversion)

Outbound XML messages must have "Outbound_Receive_Business_Request" as part of their filename
and must have the RequestID at the start of the filename followed by an _.
This is the standard filename format for the outbound business message generated by the Steria Stub

Example Outbound XML message
582_Outbound_Receive_Business_Request_15-38-05-240.xml

The converted files will be copied to the following directory where the Inbound Test App will
send it to the Steria Stub as part of Inbound Testing (whereupon the file will be moved to the sentbox)
dist\jmsutilclient-X.X.X\outbox

Note: All file conversion will occur before any inbound messages are sent from the Inbound Test App
to the Steria Stub for testing allowing for bulk testing

Whether conversion is performed and the conditions under which it is done will be controlled 
by command line parameters passed into the executable class:

-b The value of this parameter specifies the Directory where XML messages that require converting can be found. 
If -b not specified then no conversion will occur 
If -b is specified with no value (ie no directory is specified)
then the following directory will be searched for appropriate Outbound XML messages for conversion:
dist\jmsutilclient-X.X.X\conversion

-g This is boolean and so has no value 
If this parameter is specified the Inbound Test App will convert 
outbound messages to Inbound "normal" messages, 
If not specified all outbound messages will be converted to Inbound exception messages with a RelatesTo field unless -y is present. 
Note: When Inbound exception messages are generated the <error:RelatesTo> within the file will be updated
<error:RelatesTo><MessageIdentifier>582</MessageIdentifier></error:RelatesTo>

-y This is boolean and so has no value 
If this parameter is specified the Inbound Test App will convert 
outbound messages to Inbound "normal" messages with no RelatesTo field, 
If not specified all outbound messages will be converted to Inbound exception messages with a RelatesTo field unless -g is present.
Note: When Inbound exception messages are generated the <error:RelatesTo> within the file will be updated
<error:RelatesTo><MessageIdentifier>582</MessageIdentifier></error:RelatesTo>
	
-j The value of this parameter specifies the Directory where example and template messages can be found
If -j is not specified or is specified with no value then the following directory will be used when searching for examples or templates:
dist\jmsutilclient-X.X.X\conversion
Note: where converting messages to exception messages an Exception example (eg 9998MessageRECEIVEERROR.txt) 
must be in this directory

-i This represents the Starting ID used in the filename of converted inbound message files
During any one execution of the Inbound Test App it will be incremented for each message converted
The ID built into the name of the inbound message file will eventually be used to create
the GDG_INBOUND_MESSAGES record on the GDGATE database on the SCJSE Gateway and as this must be
unique it is expected that the Starting ID must be changed with each subsequent execution of
the Inbound Test App. The default setting is 1. Do not specify the parameter and leave with no value

Also to control throughput from the Inbound Test App
when there are large numbers of files to convert and send as part of a bulk test the following parameter
can be specified:
-a This is the built in delay (in ms) between sending inbound messages from the Inbound Test App
to the Steria Stub (in ms). Do not specify the parameter and leave with no value
If not specified it is set to 300ms, which will lead to an approximate throughput of 10000 inbound messages / hour


Example 
This assumes the Steria Stub is a single Weblogic Instance

Test Data: Converting an Outbound XML Message to an Inbound Exception Message
The following Outbound XML message (which is an EVENT) requires conversion and has
been added to dist\jmsutilclient-X.X.X\conversion
582_Outbound_Receive_Business_Request_15-38-05-240.xml

Test 1
To Convert to an Inbound exception message where the delay between each message is 500ms,
the Starting ID is 3000 and the example and conversion directories are the default values

jmsutilclient.bat 130.177.3.71:7071 scjsegateway/jms/InboundTestQueue 500 3000
%JAVA_HOME%\bin\java.exe %JAVA_OPTIONS% -classpath %CLASSPATH% jmsutil.Main -q %1 -d %2 -a %3 -i %4 -b -m -s

Should you wish you can specify alternate locations for the example and conversion directory
jmsutilclient.bat 130.177.3.71:7071 scjsegateway/jms/InboundTestQueue 500 3000 D:\Test_Convert_Messages_Box D:\Test_Examples_Box
%JAVA_HOME%\bin\java.exe %JAVA_OPTIONS% -classpath %CLASSPATH% jmsutil.Main -q %1 -d %2 -a %3 -i %4 -b %5 -j %6 -m -s

This will create the following file in dist\jmsutilclient-X.X.X\outbox
3000MessageRECEIVEERROR.xml

Internally the file will be an XML structure following the Exception.xsd format.
The <error:RelatesTo> will be set as follows:
<error:RelatesTo><MessageIdentifier>582</MessageIdentifier></error:RelatesTo>


Test 2
To Convert to an Inbound exception message where the delay between each message is 500ms,
the Starting ID is 5000 and the example and conversion directories are the default values
The RelatesTo field will not be part of the Inbound Message

jmsutilclient.bat 130.177.3.71:7071 scjsegateway/jms/InboundTestQueue 500 3000
%JAVA_HOME%\bin\java.exe %JAVA_OPTIONS% -classpath %CLASSPATH% jmsutil.Main -q %1 -d %2 -a %3 -i %4 -b -y -m -s

Should you wish you can specify alternate locations for the example and conversion directory
jmsutilclient.bat 130.177.3.71:7071 scjsegateway/jms/InboundTestQueue 500 3000 D:\Test_Convert_Messages_Box D:\Test_Examples_Box
%JAVA_HOME%\bin\java.exe %JAVA_OPTIONS% -classpath %CLASSPATH% jmsutil.Main -q %1 -d %2 -a %3 -i %4 -b %5 -j %6 -m -s

This will create the following file in dist\jmsutilclient-X.X.X\outbox
5000MessageRECEIVEERROR.xml

Internally the file will be an XML structure following the Exception.xsd format.
The <error:RelatesTo> will be absent


Test 3: Converting an Outbound XML Message to an Inbound "Normal" Message
To Convert to an Inbound "normal" message where the delay between each message is 200ms,
the Starting ID is 4000 and the example and conversion directories are the default values

jmsutilclient.bat 130.177.3.71:7071 scjsegateway/jms/InboundTestQueue 200 4000
%JAVA_HOME%\bin\java.exe %JAVA_OPTIONS% -classpath %CLASSPATH% jmsutil.Main -q %1 -d %2 -a %3 -i %4 -b -g -m -s

Should you wish you can specify alternate locations for the example and conversion directory
jmsutilclient.bat 130.177.3.71:7071 scjsegateway/jms/InboundTestQueue 500 3000 D:\Test_Convert_Messages_Box D:\Test_Examples_Box
%JAVA_HOME%\bin\java.exe %JAVA_OPTIONS% -classpath %CLASSPATH% jmsutil.Main -q %1 -d %2 -a %3 -i %4 -b %5 -j %6 -g -m -s

This will create the following file in dist\jmsutilclient-X.X.X\outbox
4000MessageXHIBITEVENT.xml

Note: If outbound message is of a different type this will always be included as the last part of the name
eg
4001MessageXHIBITNewCaseMessage.xml
